claims.text: Augmenting conventional EAM potentials with correction terms derived from ab initio MD displacement covariance matrices will significantly improve phase-space overlap with the ab initio liquid.
The proposed hybrid potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch to below approximately 5 meV/atom.
AlCoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloys have established baseline EAM potentials applicable in both solid and liquid states.
The method is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys over approximately 0.95–1.05 T_m.
Atomic-displacement covariance matrices can be extracted from ensembles generated by ab initio molecular dynamics.
Displacement covariance information can be incorporated as a correction to an EAM potential.
Displacement covariance matrices capture many-body and anharmonic interactions in a liquid high-entropy alloy.
Under the Gaussian approximation, covariance-based terms include anharmonic effects through their covariance values.
The covariance-based correction will enable the EAM model to represent the configurational diversity of the liquid.
Representing more of the liquid's configurational diversity will reduce reference–target phase-space mismatch and improve thermodynamic integration.
Conventional TOR-TILD EAM references do not include the proposed displacement-covariance corrections.
Conventional TOR-TILD EAM references exhibit larger integration-path errors because they insufficiently sample the relevant atomic configurations.
High-entropy alloy systems with substantially different chemical or vibrational behavior will require recalibration or further modification of the method.
The magnitude of the improvement will depend on covariance-estimation accuracy and the alloy's inherent anharmonicity.
A mismatch below approximately 5 meV/atom is supported by theoretical expectations.
